name: profile
label: Primary user
description: Who the agent works for: name, contact addresses, family and relationships, a health record with a dated weight log, tastes and work, each in its own expandable section - plus a credentials manager for site logins and TOTP secrets, encrypted with Windows DPAPI for this user. The agent reads the profile through me_profile and may use a saved login only through cred_secret / cred_totp, which ask first and are audited.

steps: Open Apps > Primary user. Each section is a fold-out box: identity, contact, family, health, tastes, work, notes. Save is per section, so a half-filled page is fine. The profile lives in jobs\profile.json and the agent gets the short version (name, preferred name, email, phone, WhatsApp, work, family) in its system prompt on every run, so it knows what "my email" means without being told.
Health is a record, not a form

Height, weight, blood type, conditions, allergies and medications are the standing facts; the log is dated entries (date, weight, note) so a trend exists without a second app. The agent can add to either with me_save, which asks first.

Add a site with its login URL, username, password and (optionally) a TOTP secret in base32. The password and the TOTP secret are encrypted with Windows DPAPI for this user - the file is useless on another machine or as another account. show and code reveal one value at a time; every read is appended to jobs\profile-audit.log. The agent can only reach them through cred_secret and cred_totp, both ask-policy tools, and cred_list shows names and usernames but never a secret.

Tools: me_profile (allow - the whole profile, no secrets), me_save (ask), cred_list (allow - names only), cred_secret and cred_totp (ask, audited), cred_save (ask). A run that needs to log in asks for the password, gets a code, and the ask is the approval you see in Chat.
fixes: The agent still asks who I am

It reads jobs\profile.json at the start of each run. If the file is empty the prompt block is omitted, so fill in at least the name; a run that started before you saved keeps the old prompt until it finishes. The tool me_profile always reads the file fresh.
It was saved by a different Windows account (DPAPI is per user) or the machine was rebuilt - the ciphertext cannot be unsealed. Save the credential again as the same user that runs PowerAgent.

The secret must be the base32 setup key, not the six-digit code and not an otpauth:// URI (paste the part after secret=). Codes are six digits, 30 seconds, SHA1 - the same as an authenticator app; if the site uses a different period or digits, this generates the standard one only.
The agent used a credential without me seeing it

cred_secret and cred_totp are ask-policy tools, so each call is an approval in Chat, and jobs\profile-audit.log records name and time. If that log shows a read you did not approve, remove the credential - the secret is gone with it.
